title: Marcos Confirms 'Provisional Understanding' on Sierra Madre Resupply, Says China Oil-and-Gas Talks 'Moved Forward'
detail: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., speaking to foreign correspondents in Manila on August 14, 2026, confirmed for the first time in his own words a 'provisional understanding' with Beijing covering resupply missions to BRP Sierra Madre at Second Thomas Shoal, while insisting this does not mean Manila is seeking China's permission or surrendering sovereignty. Marcos also said joint oil-and-gas exploration talks with China had 'moved forward,' with momentum building around potential gas deposits in the Reed Bank amid Middle East-driven oil-price volatility: 'We have to find new ways... this discussion has gained prominence. And where we are now, I think we have moved forward.' Marcos called China 'our friend' and 'one of the biggest investors still in the Philippines,' while separately ruling out allowing US forces to use Philippine territory as a staging ground against China in a Taiwan contingency.

title: China's Ministry of Natural Resources Issues First Comprehensive Ecological Bulletin on Disputed Reefs, Says Sandy Cay Coral Down 70% Since 2016 — Blames Philippines
detail: China's Ministry of Natural Resources published a 2025 marine ecological bulletin on August 14, 2026 covering nine islands and reefs across the Paracels, Spratlys and Scarborough Shoal (Zhongsha), which it called the 'first comprehensive assessment' of the area. The report found conditions 'generally good but displaying marked differences': the Xisha (Paracel) group is showing positive recovery, Huangyan Dao (Scarborough) has 135 recorded coral species with 38.8% live coral coverage in protected zones, and most Nansha (Spratly) reefs are in good condition. It flagged severe exceptions — live coral coverage at Tiexian Jiao (Sandy Cay), near Philippine-held Thitu Island, has fallen roughly 70% since 2016, which Beijing attributed to crown-of-thorns starfish outbreaks, cyclones and 'illegal' Philippine construction and fishing activity at Thitu; Ren'ai Jiao (Second Thomas Shoal) was also cited for pollution and debris reducing coral cover. The ministry said China invested over 21.3 billion yuan in 262 marine restoration projects and designated 2.66 million hectares of conservation areas from 2021-2025. The report was released as Washington and Beijing continue to spar over China's 'nature reserve' designation at Scarborough Shoal, which the US State Department has called a destabilizing pretext for territorial control.

media.caption: Live coral coverage at Sandy Cay (Tiexian Jiao) has dropped nearly 70% since 2016, China's Ministry of Natural Resources says
